comment:
We fully support advocating for a recurrent line item in national health budget to signal government ownership of DPI-H. 

In addition to payment for recurrent domestic costs of running these systems, contributions to the technologies that underpin their DPI-H, particularly for digital public goods, would be strategic, cost-efficient, and risk free means for maintaining the technologies long-term. Contributions may take the form of DPG capacity building, feature suggestions, or in-kind support to the national innovation ecosystem around DPGs.

One direct contribution model, now underway through DHIS2 Shared Services Fee, offers a novel global funding strategy to sustain the digital public goods of DPI-H. If a country contributes even marginally to a pooled fund, then it directly contributes to a stake in  platform governance, security, and maintenance, which will have downstream benefits for their national DPI-H. We note tha without a durable funding stream for digital public goods, countries will either need to accept the long-term risk of product degradation, or turn to proprietary software vendors, which have been shown by evidence to be more costly on aggregate.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
